claims.proposition_evaluated: The $100 million approved in December 2022 for capital profile CM-20-0330 is almost double the City of Edmonton's adopted 2022 gross Snow and Ice Control expenditure budget.
claims.interpretation_notes: The approved operating budget prints the 2022 Snow and Ice Control Expenditure & Transfers cell as $64.466 million ($64,466 in thousands). The resulting ratio is $100 million / $64.466 million = 1.551. Under the brief's primary cutoffs, this is Partially supported: the amount is substantially larger, but the specific phrase "almost double" fails because 1.551 is below 1.8. It is also Partially supported under the alternative cutoffs. Alternative A adds council's July 4, 2022 one-time $4.7 million increase, producing an amended gross budget of $69.166 million and a ratio of 1.446; that is Contradicted under the primary cutoffs and Partially supported under the alternative cutoffs. The published $60.9 million 2023 snow-clearing figure produces a ratio of 1.642, Partially supported under both cutoff sets; the consulted record did not establish with sufficient precision whether that fact-sheet figure incorporates every December 2022 amendment to the named program cell. The comparison mixes a four-year capital authorization with one year of operating expenditure. On a like-for-like 2023 basis, CM-20-0330's approved $5.950 million allocation was 9.77% of the published $60.9 million snow budget, not approximately double. The profile's approved allocations, printed in thousands, were $5.950 million in 2023, $26.750 million in 2024, $33.650 million in 2025 and $33.650 million in 2026, averaging $25 million per approved year. The $100 million divided by the 2022 net operating requirement of $63.653 million is 1.571. Reported CM-20-0330 actuals were $0.807 million in 2023 and $9.689 million in 2024, calculated as $10.496 million cumulative at 2024 year-end less $0.807 million cumulative at 2023 year-end. Cumulative actual expenditure was $25.093 million at September 30, 2025, implying $14.597 million during January-September 2025. Against gross Snow and Ice Control actual expenditure, the completed-year ratios were $0.807 million / $51.750 million = 1.56% for 2023 and $9.689 million / $64.749 million = 14.96% for 2024. The completed-year CM-20-0330 actual average for 2023-2024 was $5.248 million per year. A spring 2025 adjustment transferred $0.430 million from CM-20-0330, reducing its current budget to $99.570 million; it does not change what council approved in December 2022.

claims.proposition_evaluated: Under the brief's prescribed roads-only profile boundary, Edmonton's adopted 2023-2026 capital budget allocated approximately $1.8 billion to roads—about eighteen times the $100 million approved for CM-20-0330.
claims.interpretation_notes: Summing the prescribed adopted profile amounts produces $1.945703 billion: $1.116532 billion in profiles labelled Roads, $722.289 million in profiles labelled Neighbourhood Renewal and $106.882 million for the three included vehicle-carrying bridge profiles without a service-category label. The ratio to $100 million is 19.457. This is Supported under both the primary and alternative cutoffs. The required alternative is Table 8's combined "Active Pathways and Roads Service" allocation of $1.7940 billion, or 17.94 times; it is also Supported under both cutoff sets but is not a roads-only total and includes active-pathway funding. The primary exceeds the combined service line because the brief's profile-label boundary also captures profiles presented under separate service or transformational lines, including Traffic Safety and Yellowhead Trail work. The narrowest Roads-labelled-only reading is $1.116532 billion, or 11.165 times, which is Partially supported under both cutoff sets. The widest prescribed reading adds six streetscape and pedestrian profiles totalling $80.145 million, producing $2.025848 billion, or 20.258 times, Supported under both cutoff sets. Primary profiles and adopted amounts, in millions of Canadian dollars with Appendix A profile pages, are: 18-66-6503 $94.202 (p.537); 19-22-9006 $161.021 across its $119.200 and $41.821 lines (p.600); 21-20-9301 $54.634 (p.645); 21-20-9302 $54.597 (p.647); 21-40-9031 $0.012 (p.643); 21-40-9032 $0.010 (p.589); 22-22-9700 $10.056 (p.532); 22-22-9701 $5.094 (p.561); CM-20-2020 $9.007 (p.628); CM-22-0000 $64.843 (p.619); CM-24-0000 $209.836 (p.613); CM-26-0000 $9.308 (p.636); CM-66-2194 $0.720 (p.594); CM-66-2525 $16.000 (p.603); CM-66-2585 $25.875 (p.434); CM-66-2596 $17.148 (p.430); CM-99-0060 $7.914 (p.653); CM-99-9600 $376.255 (p.650); 20-40-9017 $4.658 (p.412); 20-40-9019 $0.721 (p.424); 21-40-9023 $14.652 (p.421); 21-40-9024 $22.047 (p.409); 21-40-9025 $9.780 (p.415); 21-40-9026 $2.100 (p.418); 21-40-9027 $0.464 (p.406); 22-40-9028 $17.130 (p.403); 22-40-9029 $23.710 (p.427); CM-25-0000 $545.717 (p.443); CM-27-0000 $81.310 (p.438); 23-24-0300 $97.000 (p.567); 21-24-9301 $9.832 (p.573); and 21-24-9302 $0.050 (p.564). No category-label discrepancy from the editor's declared membership was found. Widest-only additions are 21-50-9101 $0.560 (p.526), 21-50-9100 $25.400 (p.529), 17-74-4103 $0.265 (p.570), CM-20-3102 $10.100 (p.554), CM-20-3100 $13.615 (p.585) and 20-20-2024 $30.205 (p.558). The quotation says "180 times," but $1.8 billion divided by $100 million is 18, not 180; the normalized proposition appropriately evaluates the implied eighteen-fold ratio. CM-20-0330 represents 1.390% of the adopted $7.192540 billion 2023-2026 capital budget. The City separately describes it as about 2% of approximately $5 billion in transportation projects.

Narrowest Roads-labelled-only reading: $1.116532 billion, or 11.165 times.
